These improvements in absorption occur without the additional thickness of the crystal contributing to light absorption, but rather by trapping light inside the film.

We have derived a set of holomorphic functions, denoted by $\beta_{\lambda,\mu} (s)$, which, when the absolute value of $s$ tends to infinity in the right half-plane, behave similarly to iterated exponentials. These functions are linked to nested exponentials through a useful functional equation and have a series expansion that converges within a certain region of the complex plane. By examining the properties of $\beta$, we can study the dynamics of the exponential map $e^{\mu z}$ and obtain insights into the behavior of fractional iterations. Our analysis allows us to identify conditions under which Abel equations can be constructed from $\beta$ and to identify holomorphic functions of period $2\pi i / \lambda$ that serve as holomorphic Abel functions of the form $t(s+1) = e^{\mu t(s)}$.

We have developed a novel method of constructing high dimensional expanders by utilizing covering spaces of simplicial complexes. Building upon expander graphs, high dimensional expanders play a vital role in theoretical computer science but unfortunately, there are only a few constructions available that offer arbitrarily small local spectral expansion.

Our research involves presenting a probabilistic algorithm that takes a simplicial complex, g, and a sub-complex, K, and ensures that the covering graph, Γ, of g has near exponential volume growth in sparsified form, Δ, preserving edges from K, when the input graph is a contraction of the input complex, preserving the sub-complex. This algorithm also shows that the resulting sparsed graph, Δ, has a spectral expansion of o(log^2 k) when compared to the original graph, Γ.

Using our algorithm, we've developed a new construction of high dimensional expanders by utilizing expanders, Δ, with large g but with a spectral expansion of less than k^2. This construction has been proven to be the first method of constructing high dimensional expanders independently of constant local spectral expansion.

Notably, our algorithm also offers an alternative method of constructing high dimensional expanders in the case where the number of dimensions is a prime number. This is because the algorithm relies on an inverter, E, whose properties can be utilized to construct a new expander, Δ, even in the case of prime dimensions. However, this has the disadvantage of offering a constant level of

Researchers investigated the crystal and magnetic characteristics of the single-crystal, hexagonal GdInO3 through an integrated approach that combined experimental and theoretical analysis. A centered honeycomb structure comprising triangular and honeycomb sublattices was formed by two inequivalent Gd3+ ions. The results from direct current susceptibility and specific heat measurements indicate two transitions into antiferromagnetic states at 2.3 K and 1.02 K. Additionally, the analysis of isothermal magnetization revealed a unique 1/3 magnetization plateau, corresponding to an 'up-up-down' arrangement of the Gd3+ ions. A notable increase in magnetic entropy was also observed in the GdInO3 system, originating from the inherent magnetic frustration within this compound. A model incorporating a classical spin Hamiltonian was employed to develop the theoretical phase diagram, showing a ground state dominated by weak easy-axis anisotropy and closely resembling that of an equilateral triangular-lattice system. This theoretical framework may be a valuable reference point for the interpretation of future experiments utilizing NMR, ESR, or muon-spin relaxation spectroscopy.

Research into graph embedding has been gaining momentum for its applications in predicting network links on complex graphs. Many studies have highlighted the challenges of representing nodes in sparse networks effectively, as these networks often feature lengthy paths between connected nodes. These challenges have been overlooked in much of the existing work, which often focuses on more dense networks. Our proposed project, Sparse Structure Neural Network-Enabled Node embedding (SSNE), addresses this limitation by developing a universal node representation model for predicting network links in sparse networks. Our model incorporates a novel self-learning mechanism to capture the properties of prey nodes and their neighbors in pre-training, as well as a novel edge-based post-training process that enhances the prediction of existing edges. Our experiments demonstrate SSNE's superiority over existing link prediction approaches, achieving a remarkable 20% improvement in terms of accuracy.

A low-cost water jet process is employed to create a double-walled silicon cell suitable for holding atomic gases, thus offering a compact solution for in-place atom production and population manipulation. Typically, deep silicon cells are fabricated through the use of deep reactive ion etching, a method influenced by light absorption in the silicon wall. Using the water jet process eliminates this constraint, allowing for the creation of cells up to 15mm in length without stringent lighting conditions. Although not achievable through conventional surface micromachining, this advances the development of complete atomic systems integrated onto a chip.

We evaluate the precision of a recently proposed nonlinear interference model for a wide range of dual-polarization 4D formats, exhibiting an average disparity with split-step Fourier simulations of no more than 0.1 dB.

Preemptive wildfire detection is critical for minimizing ecological harm, property damage, and human loss. Recent advances in satellite and drone imaging have improved the efficiency of wildfire monitoring, especially through the use of visible and infrared data. Recent research has explored the use of deep learning and fusion techniques to enhance wildfire detection. Although fusion techniques have been found useful, they often overlook the temporal aspect of change in image sequences. This paper introduces a novel deep learning-based fusion architecture, incorporating spatial and temporal coherence constraints. This approach utilizes two types of fusion strategies: a patch-level fusion approach using a patch-by-patch convolutional neural network, and a whole-image level fusion approach using a supervised multi-input generative adversarial network. This architecture leverages the details provided by two different modalities, as well as their combination. The method captures temporal changes in sequential images by using a constraint that imposes spatial and temporal regularizations on the generated image. This approach demonstrated superior performance when tested on datasets from two wildfires, significantly improving the accuracy of small and large objects in both modalities. The implementation details are available on GitHub at https://github.com/ashish12/FIRe-GAN.

Early detection and treatment of depression is essential to prevent severe repercussions, making the utilization of multiple detection methods necessary, particularly when they do not rely on physical examinations.  Observing social media expression patterns is highly advantageous for identifying mental health, since individuals tend to convey their emotions openly on these platforms.  While current systems utilize social media data to diagnose mental health, accurately gauging depression levels is vital for informed treatment decisions.  Therefore, we developed a two-fold approach to assess and compare the effectiveness of current techniques in detecting depression levels and diagnosing the condition.  First, we gathered a large dataset consisting of 20k social media posts from 12k users, along with their depression levels, categorized into categories 0-3.  Second, we trained multiple machine learning models, including lightGBM, XGBoost, and random forest, using our dataset to test the performance of three detection methods - symptom-specific, keyword-based, and graded - utilizing the same data.  Our results reveal the effectiveness of each technique, with the graded approach yielding superior results, underscoring the importance of incorporating depression severity detection methods to support informed treatment decisions and the design of personalized intervention strategies for early depression detection.

We've developed two probabilistic models for the COVID-19 pandemic. We've derived the statistical properties of these models, including correlation functions and probability distributions. These models, which build on existing work and incorporate lockdown measures and the critical role of hospitals and health care facilities, enable us to simulate two scenarios. One scenario considers the SIS model, which assumes susceptible and infectious populations, under lockdown measures. In contrast, the other scenario includes the SIS model, which also accounts for hospitals and healthcare facilities under lockdown measures. We found that if lockdown measures are implemented, the pandemic will gradually decline over time. However, if such measures are neglected, the pandemic will continue to grow, potentially exceeding available hospital capacity and resulting in a significant increase in fatalities. This underscores the importance of immediate, widespread lockdown measures to mitigate the spread of the virus.

The ISGMR and a $K = 0$ component of the ISGQR in severely deformed nuclei exhibit a strong interrelation, manifesting as a distinctive double peak structure in the isoscalar monopole (IS0) strength distribution. A specific low-energy deformation-induced peak, alongside the broad main ISGMR peak, is identified in this relation. This letter demonstrates that an coupled IS0-IS2 channel has a substantial influence on the IS0 strength distribution, producing a double-peaked structure in nuclei such as $^{24}$Mg and $^{28}$Si where an IS0-IS2 coupling is significant. Conversely, experiments on nearly spherical nuclei like $^{12}$C and $^{16}$O reveal a broad IS0 strength distribution, indicative of negligible IS0-IS2 coupling in these systems.

A study on stick-slip dynamics and the convergence of motion paths in systems governed by Coulomb friction is conducted. The existence of a universally accessible and attractive region, near an equilibrium state, is confirmed through analytical means. Theoretical findings reveal that the system can only converge asymptotically, involving multiple sequences of stick-slip cycles, regardless of the starting conditions. Numerical simulations validate the theoretical models through diverse examples.

A crucial task in algorithmic trading involves calculating the future value of cash flows in a contract based on the current market prices, which can be achieved through a dynamic programming approach within a framework known as breaking-even analysis. This study provides the first comprehensive mathematical framework for training neural networks from such analysis and demonstrates that a specific type of network called a neural quantity network, which determines outputs by applying a permutation that accounts for signed inequalities, is effective in approximating dynamic programming value functions. Notably, our results also highlight how to incorporate flexibility into these functions by leveraging market maker techniques and show that neural quantity networks have the ability to convey uncertainty through an interval calculation method called the deep Bellman hedge. Furthermore, our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of neural quantity networks and the deep Bellman hedge approach in real-world financial contexts, specifically in managing risk in short selling tasks.

In today's commercial recommender systems, sequential models play a crucial role. These models predict the items users are most likely to engage with by analyzing their previous platform interactions. Despite their importance, many of these models struggle to grasp the underlying motivations driving users' actions online, making intent modeling vital for user understanding and optimal long-term engagement. We've developed a novel approach to probabilistically model user intent using variational autoencoders and inferred latent variables, effectively distinguishing between causal and correlation-based recommendations. We've also created a new user intent divergence metric to evaluate and refine our model. After testing our approach on a real-world Amazon order dataset, we discovered that intent modeling enhances overall ranking quality and provides valuable insights, allowing us to identify intended and diverted user actions.

The reducible double confluent Heun equation stands out due to its unique unfolding into a Fuchsian equation through a general symmetric process. The Fuchsian equation resulting from the unfolding of this particular DCHE has five distinct singular points: three located near a vanishing parameter value, one corresponding to infinity, and another positioned at its reciprocal, as well as a fifth point at infinity. The monodromy matrix of the equation near a specific regular resonant singularity at the origin can be demonstrated to emerge as a limiting product of the monodromy matrices at singular points resulting from the unfolding of the equation's parameters. The monodromy matrix near another irregular singularity at the origin shows a specific limit behavior relative to one of these parameters. The given DCHE is shown to support a globally holomorphic solution within the extended complex space when the equation is of specific rank across various singular points. The solution exhibits a characteristic dependence on the equation's specific rank across these points. The given DCHE is shown to the equivalent to a specific Fuchsian equation with distinct singularities located at the zeros of the equation's uniformization. The given equation is of specific rank in the vicinity of a regular singularity with a particular infrared fixed point, as shown through the application of the infrared criterion. The given equation is of specific rank in the vicinity of another irregular singularity with a particular flow toward this fixed point. The given equation is shown to the equivalent to a specific Heun

Low-rank matrix recovery issues with complex structures are highly relevant in real-world contexts, particularly when data exhibits rank-one heteroskedastic patterns across distinct group labels. In this scenario, the objective is to recover the underlying low-rank matrix from noisy observations, while accounting for labeled data that incorporates both noisy observations and accurate label information. Unfortunately, the current tensor methods fail to address group-wise heteroskedasticity and cannot handle labeled data, leaving the field with significant gaps. To address this challenge, the goal is to develop and analyze new algorithms that incorporate labeled data, while taking into account the group-wise heteroskedasticity. In this study, the primary focus is on the estimation of a low-rank matrix from noisy observations under group-wise heteroskedasticity without the assumption of independence. By leveraging fundamental statistical and algorithmic limits, the study demonstrates the optimal trade-offs between estimation accuracy and labeling efficiency. Notably, the findings reveal the critical role that labeled data plays in matrix estimation, particularly when compared to its counterpart in the unstructured setting. Furthermore, the study introduces a multi-stage spectral algorithm capable of achieving the optimal trade-offs by leveraging both labeled data and its structural heteroskedasticity properties.

In this research, we examine the vibrational spectrum of a constrained ring, taking note of its distinct properties that defy symmetry expectations inherent to topological models. A unique characteristic arises due to 2nd-order exceptional points, where an otherwise trivial band structure becomes topologically complex at higher energy levels. Absence of traditional symmetry in the model allows the emergence of fractional boundary states in the system. Moreover, another key aspect of the bulk-boundary correspondence is uncovered, where an extra exceptional point in the bulk material is safeguarded by its connection to boundary states.

We introduce the semi-inclusive Lepton Flavour Universality ratio $R_\Sigma$ to verify electron-to-muon universality in the $b\to s\ell^+\ell^-$ process at $e^+e^-$ B-meson facilities. This combined observable enhances our capacity to detect potential violations of short distance origin Lepton Flavour Universality and provides a more sensitive test than individual angular variables, especially for $\ell_\tau$ flavours. Additionally, $R_\Sigma$ can aid in determining the magnetic properties of charm quarks.

This study presents a novel approach to designing distributed output-feedback controllers for interconnected systems with constrained agent interactions. Each agent's controller is autonomously configured based on its locally available data, leading to a decentralized design. Importantly, our approach can maintain stability even in the face of dynamic network reconfigurations, without requiring adjustments from other agents, thus ensuring seamless integration of new members and efficient controller upkeep. This robust design is enabled by leveraging Bass' algorithm to compute stabilizing controller gains through distributed solutions to Lyapunov equations.

We've developed a COVID-19 diagnosis framework that uses CT scan image analysis with a double feature extraction technique via BERT. The initial step utilizes a 3D-CNN to extract spatial information from the CT images and then employs BERT for temporal aggregation of these features. A classification model is trained on the combined data, enabling the network to learn how to represent the scans as input into a subsequent model that predicts COVID-19 status. By using this approach on a smaller dataset, we've demonstrated improved accuracy on a larger dataset in comparison to using just 3D-CNN features.

Network science is the multidisciplinary study of intricate systems, which can be represented as interconnected networks consisting of nodes and edges with various attributes. These seemingly straightforward structures conceal an extraordinary depth of complexity due to their capability to encapsulate a wide array of real-world phenomena, encompassing chemical reactions, biological pathways, social connections, and other intricate relationships. Mastering network science necessitates the mastery of a fundamental tool set, encompassing statistical models of the network topology, its node and edge characteristics, as well as an array of sophisticated algorithms for network analysis and visualization. At the core of this discipline lie pressing inquiry questions, seeking to unravel the underlying principles and mechanisms of the networked world. This tutorial serves as a comprehensive visual atlas, offering a unified framework for understanding, communicating, and presenting fundamental concepts, empirical observations, and theoretical models in the domain of network science. This tutorial is intended to serve as an introductory roadmap for scholars and practitioners seeking to grasp the essence of this rapidly evolving field.

The integration of paleontology, evolutionary biology, and ecology has yielded significant insights into eco-evolutionary processes, which are mutually beneficial. This synergy is evident in a special issue, 'Eco-Evolutionary Dynamics,' where the primary contributors examine the various temporal scales of eco-evolutionary development and adaptability. We begin by reviewing the unique contributions of each author and then explore the subjects within three primary areas of focus: 1) the impact of timescales and rate modifiers on eco-evolutionary transitions, 2) the development of dynamic models, and 3) the incorporation of timescale information into models that describe and predict eco-evolutionary changes. Our discussion ultimately focuses on strategic management and future research directions to effectively manage and anticipate eco-evolutionary transformations at different scales.

A recently established benchmark called SUPERB drives research into learning speech representations by comparing various speech models with minimal adjustments to improve downstream performance. By showing that self-supervised speech models can excel in multiple downstream tasks with little adaptation, SUPERB highlights a significant paradigm in the speech field that needs to be studied more. Specifically, assessing the ability of speech models to resist malicious attacks under the control of the task has significant real-world implications. Consequently, this paper aims to analyze the susceptibility of speech models to the SUPERB benchmark in the context of adversarial attacks. The authors examine two types of attacks: the first is based on the influence of the task as per the task-ambient approach, while the second is a purely acoustic threat posed by white noise. The researchers also use a novel multi-stage adversarial approach, combined with a sign-target method that modifies the speech input to achieve a target output. The results show that speech models developed for the SUPERB benchmark exhibit varying levels of vulnerability to the proposed adversarial threats, with pure self-supervised models demonstrating a high level of susceptibility to the task-ambient attack and relatively better resistance to the other two threats. Moreover, the authors demonstrate the efficacy of their adversarial approach on multiple downstream tasks with minimal data required for the attack model. With this study, the authors urge the speech community to further examine the potential of speech models to resist malicious attacks under the control of the task.

Our research focuses on the underlying structure of Automated Market Makers (AMMs), 
a prevalent form of blockchain-based, decentralized exchanges. 
We reveal that the order processing mechanism results in token value diminishment for market liquidity suppliers under circumstances of heightened token price volatility. 
AMMs are adopted predominantly when a limited number of highly liquid tokens are used across a large user base. 
We also derive a comprehensive theoretical framework for predicting the prevalence of AMMs and test its validity using empirical data from the cryptocurrency market, 
revealing that as the number of listed tokens increases, the adoption rate of AMMs declines, 
while a larger user base leads to an increased presence of AMMs. 
Furthermore, our analysis based on empirical data from CryptoCompare shows that AMMs play 
a significant role in the cryptocurrency market, particularly during periods of high volatility when many central exchanges shut down trading.

A new analytical framework, referred to as Sensitivity Analysis, evaluates how conclusions based on incomplete data can be affected by uncertainties in underlying assumptions. We build upon an existing metric known as the E-value, which measures the reliability of causal inferences made using unmeasured confounder analysis. We apply this framework to determine the sensitivity of such inferences in the context of two bayesian models used for unmeasured confounder analysis, specifically propensity score and two-stage models. Our results indicate that the choice of prior distribution in both models significantly impacts sensitivity. However, the impact of model selection, priors, and data quality is difficult to assess due to the computational intensity of the bayesian methodology. We propose a simpler approximation, referred to as the "best case scenario," which aims to minimize bias in sensitivity analysis. We demonstrate that this approximation yields reasonable outcomes in the context of unmeasured confounder analysis.

This study investigates the commutative properties of the higher-dimensional Laurent extension of the quantum plane. A comprehensive analysis involves classifying all general symmetries associated with the associated algebraic system, where the symmetries in question are elements that leave the algebraic system unchanged while also being compatible with each other. To achieve this, two distinct approaches are used. Firstly, a method involving visualization is applied to identify non-constant symmetries in lower-dimensional cases. Secondly, a more analytical approach is employed to address the challenge of finding all commutative properties in any given dimension. The resulting findings include explicit expressions for the most general symmetries in both the finite and infinite cases. Furthermore, this research also establishes a connection between these general symmetries and the solutions to the quantum version of the KZ equation. Specifically, it shows that the identified symmetries correspond to the solutions that are invariant under certain transformations, while also being expressed in a uniform manner that can be generalized to any rank.

The integration of Blockchain technology and Federated Learning models holds great promise for transforming Internet of Vehicles (IoVs) into a secure and privacy-conscious system. To leverage these benefits, vehicles can share learned models and update them collectively, while also verifying the validity and integrity of the models through a public blockchain. Considering the explosive growth in IoT devices, including IoVs, this review assembles existing research on blockchain-enabled federated learning frameworks, with a focus on IoV applications, and explores challenges, architectures, and open challenges within this field. A comprehensive review is also provided on the challenges and limitations in enabling effective BL-Fed learning in IoV networks.

The ALICE experiment has recorded the $p_\mathrm{T}$ distribution of D meson production, including both prompt and non-prompt (formed in beauty-hadron decays), in proton-proton collisions at 5.02 TeV, and focused on data with an integrated luminosity of approximately 19.3 nb^-1. D mesons were identified through their decays into different hadronic combinations, such as $\mathrm{D^0 \to K^-\pi^+}$ and $\mathrm{D_s^+\to \phi\pi^+\to K^-K^+\pi^+$, and their production cross-sections at various $p_\mathrm{T}$ thresholds were determined. Moreover, the analysis resulted in the first measurements of the production cross-sections of the $\mathrm{D^0}$ and $\mathrm{D_s^+}$ mesons in proton-proton collisions at the specified energy, and the production rates of these mesons were found to be in line with both next-to-leading-order QCD predictions and fixed-target measurements made at similar energy scales.

The rapidly advancing field of quantum computing, fueled by recent breakthroughs, is now driven to perfect itself in the rugged terrain of millikelvin temperatures.  A cutting-edge platform at the National Accelerator Laboratory will host innovative devices that harness this environment to boost their performance, led by a collaborative team including Amy Leiby, Bahaeddin Sanii, and M. J. ryan, in a mission to establish a large-scale quantum computing system.  This comprehensive assessment details the sophisticated cryogenic facility they've devised, incorporating superconductivity, radiofrequency insulation, and superconducting radiofrequency amplification, accompanied by extensive diagnostic tools, all aimed at supporting quantum computing hardware.

Previous research indicates a high prevalence of misused crypto APIs in Java and C, but similar studies for other languages have been absent, with one notable exception - a study conducted on professional developers in Python revealed a lower incidence of insecure code for crypto-related tasks. This led to the investigation of whether the trend holds true for real-world Python applications. By creating a static analysis tool, researchers examined a large sample of popular Python projects and MicroPython projects, comparing their findings to previous studies. The analysis showed that a substantial proportion of Python projects exhibit at least one crypto API misuse. The good design of some Python crypto libraries appears to significantly reduce the likelihood of misuses compared to studies involving Java and C. The analysis also revealed that while misuses are prevalent in popular Python projects, their numbers are significantly lower than those found in studies involving Java and C, with the good design of some Python crypto libraries contributing to this difference. The researchers also discovered that MicroPython projects exhibit fewer crypto API misuses compared to Python projects. The main reason for this difference appears to be the smaller codebase in MicroPython projects as well as the better design of the crypto library used in these projects.

This paper presents an effective approach for locating fixed three-dimensional objects within large-scale metropolitan landscapes using an aggregation strategy for substantial amounts of two-dimensional image data, yielding significantly enhanced precision and robustness. A decentralized voting system is utilized to reduce labeling ambiguity and facilitate efficient object localization in densely populated urban areas. The proposed method is validated through experiments on newly acquired image datasets captured by a drone, as well as on a comprehensive collection of canonical objects and the KITTI Dataset. Furthermore, the accompanying platform, VALUE, is made available to the research community at https://github.com/NRGLab/VALUE.

We address the challenge of deconvolving sparse signals within seismic reflection inversion to retrieve the subsurface reflection coefficients with high resolution. Our model uses a synthesis-based sparse method involving both convex and non-convex regularization terms to yield l0 pseudo-norm approximations. This leads to an iterative algorithm utilizing proximal averaging that can be reformatted as a trainable neural network, the NuSPAN. By integrating a suitable activation function, such as a soft thresholding function, we achieve the ability to dynamically adjust the level of l0 pseudo-norm approximations between 1 and infinity. Our method was tested using synthetic data against established inversion techniques like SPIR, SVA, and YASS, showing notable improvements in approximation error rates. Furthermore, we applied NuSPAN to real-world seismic profiles from the Pinnacle27ES dataset and achieved successful inversion results with l0 pseudo-norm approximations set to 5. Our source code for NuSPAN is publicly available on GitHub at https://github.com/zju-EES/NuSPAN.

This article investigates the semigroups of composition operators on BMOA-type spaces, specifically on BMOA_p and its analogue VMOA_p. BMOA_p is a part of the family of F(p,q,s) spaces introduced by R. Zhao and C. C. Chu in their study on the iterated integration operators' closed ranges. Our research provides sufficient conditions under which the semigroup of composition operators by beta-functions is normal or strongly continuous on VMOA_p. We also establish the essential closedness of the integration operator T in BMOA_p to Lp for 1 < p < infinity, provided the function beta showcases bounded behavior. In doing so, we expand the scope of our findings to include its application on the VMOA_p space. We have demonstrated that for the integration operator T to be bounded on BMOA_p, the condition beta being bounded is not necessarily a requirement; however, we found another class of beta functions that exhibit localized behavior at infinity while ensuring the operator T's boundedness in BMOA_p.

Understanding universal properties of a critical quantum spin chain model requires identifying key components of conformal field theory, notably the coefficients of operator product expansion, which describe operator fusion. Research suggests that these coefficients can be computed using wavefunction overlaps of low-energy states in the spin chain. We have demonstrated that central charge, conformal dimensions, and operator product expansion coefficients are encoded in wavefunction overlaps, accompanied by universal corrections that rely on cyclic orbifold CFT content. This approach allows for numerical computation of all conformal data solely based on low-energy eigenstates, a method that was verified in the Ising model and extended to other models. Additionally, this method has been applied to the Haagerup model, another critical spin chain, whose results indicate that both models exhibit similar behavior despite differing spin chain types.

Accurate part-of-speech (POS) tagging of texts from past eras is crucial for understanding language evolution, but recent methods developed for modern languages with large datasets are not always successful when applied to texts from earlier periods. Since many of these older texts lack annotated annotations, we propose a different approach. The state-of-the-art POS tagger is initially employed to generate a probability distribution of possible tags for each word, but this distribution is not necessarily a certain prediction. To address this uncertainty, we develop a method for POS tagging that considers the potential errors. The NTT corpus, which includes nearly one million tokens from 19th century Japanese texts, is used to test the reliability of the method. The results show that the probability distribution of tags can be quite uncertain, but the method is able to reduce uncertainty and improve tag accuracy. The proposed method is not exclusive to NTT corpus and can be applied to other historical language datasets as well.

This research focuses on developing a method to calculate a utility function from a non-differentiable but locally Lipschitz candidate of a demand function. Using this method, we derive two new criteria that a demand function candidate must meet. First, it must be symmetrical and have a negatively semi-definite Slutsky matrix, and second, it must be a unique concave solution to a specific partial differential equation globally. Additionally, under certain assumptions, the resulting utility function corresponds to a unique quasi-convex extreme extension of a non-differentiable but locally Lipschitz quasi-concave ordinal coherent upper semi-continuous utility function. This work is an extension of the classic integrability approach developed by Varian (1985) but is now applied to a demand function that does not have continuous second-order differentiability everywhere, instead being locally Lipschitz on every Euclidean ball.

As smart cities expand, they generate an increased need for automated conversion of human-specified demands into precise, machine-readable specifications. Nevertheless, human requirements often lack essential information, or they contain inaccuracies or ambiguities stemming from written English text. We introduce CitySpec, an innovative AI-powered system for formalizing smart city needs, which effectively bridges language and logic gaps. The purpose of this research is to explain CitySpec's functionality by showcasing three practical applications: real-time requirements conversion within a web interface, streamlining discussions via an AI-assisted chatbot, and integrating CitySpec with other leading global cities via a collaborative platform called CityPuzzle.

Our study proposes an innovative quantum error mitigation technique grounded in the hidden inverse protocol, applicable to actual superconducting quantum devices. By integrating the PECMA error mitigation strategy in the hidden inverse framework, we enhanced the peak value of the ratio of interference fringes' coherence to amplitude, increasing it nearly five times. This improved effectiveness was validated through simulations of both classical gates and quantum operations within the Jaynes-Cummings model.

In a general category $\mathbb E$, taking the direct image of a partial order under a surjective epimorphism may not yield a partial order. In the category of sets, the best partial order approximation of the image in such a case is obtained by forming the cofibered image of the original preorder above the epimorphism. In categories satisfying regularity conditions, the existence of such an upper cofibered preorder has been established in the literature. In this study, the conditions for the existence of cofibered images and equivalences in categories satisfying regularity are examined, using the concepts of relative local connectedness. Specifically, the study demonstrates the existence of the upper cofibered preorder in $1$-regular categories with a certain type of local connectedness property, while also showing the sufficiency of a less stringent local connectedness condition for the existence of the upper cofibered equivalence in these categories.

Using a joint multivariate spatial model based on the work of Heffernan and Tawn, the relationship between satellite wind speed data, wave height observations, and extreme weather patterns is examined in the North East Atlantic between 2007-2018. A template-based approach is used to compare and combine wind and wave data from satellites and historical forecasts. Analysis involves standardizing wind and wave measurements and applying an extreme value index calculation. Subsequently, a Bayesian inference procedure is employed to estimate parameters for the resulting standardised variables. Extreme events are then modeled using a spatial extreme value model, which accounts for varying extreme behavior over time, and significant correlations are found between satellite wind speed, wave height, and extreme events at specific locations. Extreme events are further linked to specific weather patterns, which were identified through a large-scale dataset analysis, revealing new insights into the spatial distribution and timing of storms and waves.

Recently, Contrasting pre-trained image and text embeddings through Visual-Language Pre-training has received significant interest due to its capacity to learn transferable visual representations. Nevertheless, its performance is limited by semantic inconsistencies between datasets. To optimize visual-textual alignment for CLIP models on various tasks, we introduce a technique that refines image-text cross-modality learning via VT-CLIP. This process involves utilizing attention-driven mechanisms to direct text features toward informative visual regions, effectively enhancing visual-textual correlation for improved category-based matching. Subsequently, we demonstrate VT-CLIP's efficacy in few-shot classification scenarios on 11 prominent datasets.

To enhance the accuracy of computational models plagued by noisy data and parameters, this study addresses the issue of reducing error in a linear system affected by uncertainty. By building upon Etter and Ying's '20 L-matrix theory, this research extends it to the general matrix category, revealing the existence of an optimal parameter that minimizes error in an invariant subspace, and develops a method to achieve this with optimal relative error using matrix operations. Additionally, this research demonstrates the potential applications of this development in the field of quantum computing, and shows that the algorithm may be implemented in a quantum setting with potential applications in a quantum setting.

We calculate the slices and the slice spectral sequence of integral suspensions of the equivariant Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra, where the spectra of the form $H\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$ are considered, and the equivariance group in question is the quaternionic group $Q_8$. In the process, we compute the Mackey functors for $\underline{\pi}_{k\rho} H\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$.

Given a Noetherian local ring with a specific prime characteristic and its primary ideal in terms of an $\mathfrak{m}$-primary parameter, we establish criteria for $F$-rationality based on the tight Hilbert function of that ideal. These criteria enable the computation of the tight Hilbert function of certain rings, specifically reduced local rings with a specific codimension and particular Cohen-Macaulay properties. As a result, we establish the $F$-rationality of such rings, showing that certain rings are $F$-rational if their tight Hilbert function meets specific conditions.

The application of machine learning in image diagnostics within pathology and radiology is undergoing significant transformation, bringing new opportunities for standardized image annotations and model outputs to be widely shared across the research and clinical communities. Currently, resources available for training and validating deep learning models are often limited by inconsistent formatting, hindering their effectiveness and portability. To address this, we have developed Highdicom, a Python library providing tools for generating and parsing DICOM data, allowing for easy standardization of image annotations and model outputs in pathology and radiology. This specification can be utilized across multiple formats, including the PyTorch Intermediate Format and JSON. By standardizing image annotations and model outputs in DICOM, researchers and clinicians can easily share and compare results using a consistent format, facilitating the dissemination of workflows and tools. This, in turn, can aid in the transfer of techniques from research to clinical applications.

We present a derivation of Noether's current from the Einstein-Hilbert action's surface term and demonstrate that the corresponding charge is connected to Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, when evaluated on the horizon. The entropy can also be calculated using a Virasoro algebra and Cardy formula approach, in which we identify relevant diffeomorphisms based on a simple physical principle that maintains the horizon structure's invariance. Our method complements earlier research and utilizes the York-Gibbons-Hawking surface term to reach a similar conclusion, thereby providing technical and physical advancements.

In recent times, deep learning models have been effectively utilized for categorizing DNA sequences based on various tasks. A major challenge often arises due to the lengthy and variable nature of these DNA sequences. In our current research, a sequence-to-sequence autoencoder model is applied and modified specifically for categorizing nonlinear DNA architecture. An additional regularization technique, in the form of DNA-basis constraints, is introduced to the traditional autoencoder approach, which we have further developed to suit mesoscale DNA structure classification. Through exhaustive experiments, our findings demonstrate that the enhanced DNA-basis sequence-to-sequence autoencoder exhibits robust performance, even when trained without labels, and may also have implications for supervised classification methods.

The manner in which the surface of materials is terminated has significant implications for their physical characteristics. Investigating the metal-insulator transition in V$_2$O$_3$ films necessitates a deep comprehension of the connection between the surface termination and electronic configuration. Our study focuses on V$_2$O$_3$ films grown on Si(111) and Al(111) substrates, achieving epitaxial growth with high quality through molecular beam epitaxy. X-ray photoemission spectroscopy reveals that the films have the correct electronic configuration, and the metal-insulator transition is accurately predicted. Our research indicates that the metal-insulator transition is influenced by the surface termination, with the transition occurring at 150 K for the VO(0001) surface, but at 205 K for the VVOH surface. These results demonstrate that the metal-insulator transition in V$_2$O$_3$ films can be controlled by selecting a suitable growth condition to produce films with the desired surface termination, thus opening new avenues in the study and development of transition metal oxides.

A new, systematic method referred to as the Clebsch canonization has been proposed for converting Lie-Poisson equations into equivalent canonical Hamiltonian systems through a momentum map connection. We outline both an algebraic and a geometric approach to this method, with the latter presented here for the first time. Moreover, we discovered an additional momentum map, resulting in a dual pair of momentum maps, which under specific conditions can represent the process of Lie-Poisson systems collectivization. Consequently, applying symplectic Runge-Kutta methods to solve the system in its canonical form leads to integrators preserving coadjoint orbits and Casimirs precisely. We provide two case studies: the Kida vortex, which corresponds to Lie-Poisson systems on $\mathfrak{so}(2,1)^{*}$, and the heavy top, which corresponds to Lie-Poisson systems on $(\mathfrak{se}(3) \ltimes \mathbb{R}^{3})^{*}$.

The team has completed a comprehensive analysis of microlensing planets identified by the KMTNet AnomalyFinder in 2018, resulting in 9 newly discovered and 8 previously known planets in the sub-prime field. Out of these 9 new planets, 6 were clearly found to have a planetary nature, whereas 3 showed ambiguous signs. Together with a separate study on 2018 prime-field planets, this research provides the first detailed examination of a complete microlensing planetary sample, exhibiting a success rate for the AnomalyFinder of approximately 80%. Notably, the discovered planets showed a range of masses, from very small to more massive objects, consistent with expectations. However, the sample revealed a lower fraction of small planets relative to larger ones compared to other datasets, possibly due to biases related to sensitivity levels or planet-star degeneracies. The findings also showed a significant underrepresentation of four planets relative to other datasets, likely due to a lack of detectable anomalies caused by lensing effects. The team's research highlighted the effectiveness of the AnomalyFinder in identifying planets, especially smaller ones, which will be crucial in determining the mass and statistical properties of the Galactic habitable zone's typical objects.

To address a category of optimal control issues for hyperbolic conservation law systems and their regularization versions through viscosity, a comprehensive approach is proposed and implemented. This approach is illustrated through the analysis of the canonical example of the barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations. Firstly, the necessary condition for entropy - entropy flux - metric in the BNS is identified and implemented. A specific metric related to the absolute continuity of the solution is found, and its relation to the Lagrangian of the system is explored. A method of measuring the metric's observability for a system of conservation laws is discovered, which leads to the implementation of a control mechanism. This control mechanism is associated with the implementation of a specific resolvent estimate, and it is found that a particular method of compactness is not necessary for the implementation of the control mechanism. Secondly, the sufficient condition for the metric observability in the BNS is implemented, which in turn leads to the implementation of a specific observability estimate for a compactly supported initial condition. This in turn leads to the implementation of a null controllability estimate under the same initial conditions. Finally, the necessary and sufficient condition for the metric observability in the BNS through a specific regularizing process is implemented, which in turn leads to the implementation of a specific observability estimate for a more general initial condition when the regularizing process is applied to the initial condition. This in turn leads the implementation of a null controllability estimate under the same conditions when

Accurately predicting non-performing loans for individual clients is a key factor for banks to minimize financial risks and maximize loan profits. This process involves collecting essential information about the client, allowing banks to base loan approval decisions on data rather than relying solely on intuition. Consequently, banks can gain a competitive edge by using data-driven approaches to mitigate the inherent danger of non-performing loans. In our study, we compared the effectiveness of several machine learning models in predicting non-performing loans for individual clients using Dataset 1 from the International Conference on Machine Learning and Analytics, 2020. Following this evaluation, we performed a feature selection analysis to determine the most crucial variables for predicting non-performing loans.

The connections between the chromatic symmetric functions of specific Dyck paths, originally discovered by Stanley and later expanded on by Shareshian-Wachs in their $q$-analogue, are crucial in their associations with Hessenberg varieties, diagonal harmonics, and LLT polynomials. Notably, for the so-called abelian Dyck paths, an unexpected relationship was also discovered in relation to the placements of non-attacking rooks in two studies, one published in 1993 by Stanley and Stembridge, and the other in 2013 by Guay-Paquet. In a subsequent development related to the $q$-analogue, Abreu and Nigro generalized the results in their 2020 study using a concept called $q$-hit numbers, an extension of the work of Han and Wu in 2017. In this present research, it is demonstrated that the HSFs of all Dyck paths can be related to the HSFs of a family of so-called alternating Dyck paths through a process in the colored framework. Specifically, this research identifies a set of "multi-hit" invariants, expressed as colored area polynomials, for each path in the studied family, and these are shown to represent combinations of the HSFs of the original paths, achieved through a process involving the placements of multi-hit rooks. As in previous studies, this research reveals that these HSFs of the altered paths are now expressing the $q$-HSFs

Deep learning models, specifically Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs), are capable of generating robust orientation representations in images, making them effective for orientation recognition tasks. Despite this capability, traditional DCNNs often require significant manual configuration and tuning of parameters, a time-consuming process for researchers. To streamline this process and improve DCNNs' ability to generalize across various orientations, we are introducing a new model called Orientation Convolution Networks (OCNs), which leverages a unique architecture and transfer learning to enhance image recognition performance. Our experimental results demonstrate that OCNs significantly outperform traditional DCNNs and other competing methods in robust orientation recognition.

Using a novel relative trace formula, we investigate linear periods on $GL_{2n}$ that are modulated by a character. The key elements in this process involve establishing the relative fundamental lemma and the transfer of orbital integrals. Coupled with the spectral isolation technique pioneered by Beuzart-Plessis--Liu--Zhang--Zhu, we derive comparisons of the elliptic aspects of the involved relative trace formulas, ultimately yielding novel outcomes that extend Waldspurger's theorem to the scenario where n is equal to 1.

We develop a systematic method to study the impact of mass on the pole mass in comparison to short-distance masses like the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ mass for a heavy quark, specifically with applications to the top quark, through renormalization in QCD up to four-loop levels. The method involves constructing a specific type of quark operator, known as the SV Z vertex, and relating it to the top quark pole mass and a matched, renormalized NRQCD $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ mass. The construction of the SV Z vertex allows us to isolate the high-energy logarithms in perturbation theory, thus minimizing their influence on the mass difference as the logarithmic term divides out when computing the mass difference. By matching the two quark masses, we translate the dependence on the pole mass to the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ mass at a specific scale $\mu$, and then use an all-orders equation to remove the remaining logarithms. The method is tested in a regime where the mass differences among the light quarks are negligible. The results for the mass differences among the top quark pole mass and the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ mass at the third-loop level confirm that incorporating five-loop perturbative renormalization effects would yield corrections to the pole mass that are less than one percent. Furthermore, we also derive a corresponding result for the $b$ quark quark.

Consider a graph $G$ and a subset $R$ of its vertices $V(G)$.  A specific type of coloring called a sequential $k$-edge coloring for the pair $(G, R)$ is defined as an even coloring of the edges of $G$ with $k$ different colors, where all the vertices in $R$ have a specific sequence of colors associated with them.  If this vertex subset is present, a sequential $k$-edge coloring for $(G, R)$ is possible when $G$ has a specific degree $\Delta(G)-1$.  We show that this particular value of $\Delta(G)$ is best possible in this case.

We establish a precise relationship between L^p to L^q contraction inequalities in weighted Bergman spaces over the unit disk, incorporating typical weight factors and α > 1. This outcome addresses an unresolved issue in reference \cite{JANSON}, with the added consideration of cases where q is greater than or equal to 2, while providing related estimates for 0 < q < 2.

Currently, the most trusted diagnostic tool for COVID-19 is RT-PCR, which
takes several days and sometimes produces incorrect results. Computed Tomography
scans can provide valuable assistance with COVID-19 diagnosis, although they expose
patients to a significant amount of radiation, which can be detrimental to those
requiring multiple scans. To address this issue, we studied low-dose and ultra-low
dose scan protocols, which minimize radiation levels while enabling more
diagnostic images. Our research focuses on identifying COVID-19 lesions in extremely
low-dose scan images by using a two-stage approach with a time-distributed capsule
network. The first stage involves local enhancement of lung lesions, and the second
stage is dedicated to accurate diagnosis using combined 3D segmentation and
classification capabilities. In experiments, our model achieved 92% diagnostic accuracy
and 92% percentage consistency with expert radiologists, who noticed that this
preliminary finding could be transferred to other tasks involving visual detection.

As numerous satellite constellations in the low-Earth orbit region are scheduled to launch, effectively utilizing the space occupied by their formations is essential. Understanding how the space in this region is distributed among all satellites and formations is crucial for preventing collisions and managing congested areas. In this research, a method for estimating the space in LEO, where satellites of varying sizes reside, is being developed by defining an occupancy volume around each satellite and calculating its occupation density. By applying this approach, the total space in LEO can be determined as the difference between the total available volume and the occupied space. By analyzing all satellites in LEO, the total space in LEO can be calculated as 2. $\times$10$^6$ km$^3$. Moreover, a space multiplier concept is introduced to assess the available space in LEO for new satellites or deployments, which is currently at 36 % for LEO.

To generate top-quality quadrilateral meshes on complex computer-aided design (CAD) models efficiently, we propose an integrated solution. A versatile mesh with numerous irregular points is initially created to cater to the diverse shapes present on the CAD model. Subsequently, an optimization problem is formulated to determine the high-quality cell divisions while adhering to the CAD model's intricate structure. Notably, our proposed approach allows for flexible mesh topology, including multiple materials and boundary regions. Several case studies are presented to showcase the effectiveness and benefits of our proposed technique, such as enhanced artistic detail and streamlined processing times for complex designs.

Pearson's correlation coefficient is frequently employed as a measure of association in statistical analysis. The strength of evidence for linear correlation is often evaluated using a hypothesis test, resulting in a p-value. Under certain data transformations and assuming normal distribution of a dataset, a corresponding p-value can be calculated as a standard normal statistic's quantile. The resulting p-values are prone to systematic errors when finite sample sizes are considered. As a result, a corrected approach, involving a transformation of data, can produce more accurate results. The corrected method generates a statistically consistent estimate for the correlation coefficient, effectively eliminating compositional shape errors, and is robust against various data arrangements. Notably, this transformed correlation coefficient is also an unbiased estimator of the population correlation. By analyzing a particular non-normal probability model, researchers can derive an exact formula to calculate the average, variance, skewness, and higher-order moments of a correlation coefficient's distribution. These calculated moments can further inform a corresponding test statistic's asymptotic distribution, offering a rigorous probabilistic framework.

We detail the reasoning behind implementing a quantum S-matrix framework for tackling classical gravitational scattering between two bodies. Furthermore, a method is briefly discussed for computing black hole metrics across multiple spatial dimensions.

We investigate the two- or three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations defined within a bounded region. This model takes into account an external force that introduces instability and is constrained by no-slip boundary conditions. The goal of our work is to stabilize such a system through finite dimensional control mechanisms in the vicinity of an unstable equilibrium in critically regulated Sobolev and Besov spaces. This research is a logical continuation of the author's earlier works, specifically [89] and [90], which dealt with localized boundary control and feedback. This study utilizes a complex, centralized approach, focusing on constructing a central stabilization function that is able to overcome the challenges of working within the critical spaces and to accurately analyze the behavior of the uncontrolled system using the Fourier restriction technique and wavelet decomposition. This study is divided into two main parts, each of which explores one of the two low-dimensional stabilization approaches in detail. This work ultimately aims to provide comprehensive insights into how stabilization techniques evolve from the most basic to the most complex forms, specifically from finite dimensional boundary control to boundary and interior control, and from the global to the interior control scenarios.

Language learning dictionaries can facilitate vocabulary acquisition by supplying 
word definitions, although conventional dictionaries may struggle with 
capturing word meanings that vary across specific contexts. A potential solution 
is introduced in this study: the LitMind Dictionary, an online dictionary platform 
accessible through a web interface. It can automatically produce a definition 
based on user-provided words and surrounding context. Furthermore, the LitMind 
Dictionary supports multilingual queries, enabling the generation of definitions 
for Chinese and English, as well as cross-language inquiries between these two 
languages. A simplified user interface enables quick comprehension of query terms 
and enhances the overall user experience. The LitMind Dictionary is open-source, 
and the code, as well as data used in its development, are openly available on 
GitHub.

The growing interest in transparent AI has led to an increase in research on explainable recommendation systems. Among these, post-hoc methods have been identified as the most practical solutions for enhancing the transparency of prediction models. A recent study demonstrated the effectiveness of a simple post-hoc technique, called LIME, in improving the integrity of item recommendation services. However, the validity of LIME's explanations relies on an external feature extraction system, which might compromise the consistency of explanations. Furthermore, the challenge of connecting the explanation to the actual user behavior poses difficulties for the training of LIME models.

In contrast to existing research, our work focuses on the training of LIME models utilizing real-time interaction data, thereby addressing the above concerns. A trained LIME model can offer item-wise explanations in conjunction with an RS. In addition, our approach utilizes feedback information to ensure that the explanation remains coherent with the user's preferences. In experiments with LIME-RS, our method has demonstrated an exceptional ability to isolate crucial features and, consequently, achieve notable enhancements in satisfaction and system adherence. Notably, when integrated with LIME-RS, our approach led to a significant 16% increase in satisfaction and system adherence, outperforming other contemporary state-of-the-art techniques.

Quantum devices based on superconducting properties may be effectively produced
using semiconductor-superconductor hybrids, consisting of materials in close
contact and a well-formed connection. The surface energy levels of materials like
InAs, characterized by a narrow band gap, are specifically positioned near the
top of the material's conduction band. The quantum wells of the same type exhibit
a thin-layer structure growing on a substrate. The movement of charges within
these surface quantum wells is influenced by a large conduction band density of
states and the movement of charges is restricted near the surface of the material,
causing an increase in the position of the surface energy levels. The position of
these surface energy levels can be evaluated using the vibration properties of
the materials, under a bias of specific charges, and when superconducting properties
are examined, it becomes clear that the surface energy levels are positioned
very close to the conduction band edge. The position of these surface energy
levels can also be controlled by introducing a thin layer of a material with
characterized energy properties that are flexible, like AlO$_x$, which can adaptively
change the position of these surface energy levels, thereby facilitating the
establishment of a stable connection between the materials.

Research has shown that certain distributional assumptions enable learning from label queries in complex environments, but these assumptions do not extend to robust learning in general. We investigate the concept of local stability in class conditional problems and provide the first non-trivial results for learning in a semi-supervised setting where the target distribution is unknown. We demonstrate that local stability facilitates learning from label queries in a wide range of settings, including complex environments, but also establish lower bounds on the number of necessary queries in different scenarios. Furthermore, we examine the effect of noisy data and noisy stability queries in a model that integrates both sources of information, revealing that query noise can be mitigated by maintaining access to both noisy data and stability queries. Finally, we compare the efficiency of learning from stability queries in a fully unsupervised model to an existing method that relies solely on stability labels and shows that our approach yields significantly superior results in a range of experiments.

Our previous research significantly enhanced the computational efficiency of the Sinkhorn algorithm by reducing the complexity of a key kernel from quadratic to linear with the number of dimensions. This breakthrough enabled us to develop a novel iterative solver for the Sinkhorn algorithm, where each iteration recalculates the optimal scaling and the penalized kernel in O(N) time instead of the traditional N^2. This advancement leads to faster convergence, as demonstrated by our new solver's performance in the kernel gallery. Based on this theory, we have created a new Sinkhorn solver and our results show that this new solver outperforms the state-of-the-art solutions when applied to large-scale problems in the field of optimal transport.

Young stars emitting intense X-ray and UV radiation can drastically alter planetary atmospheres, influencing both mass loss and chemistry, which might have a significant impact on the potential for supporting liquid water and potentially life on exoplanets. Observing AU Mic, a 22-million-year-old star with planetary candidates, can provide significant insights due to its proximity and strong stellar radiation. Our study involves analyzing over 320 EUVE spectra, facilitating an investigation into the star's FUV emission. Observations of AU Mic's FUV radiation suggest a strong dependence on spectral type and age, with a notable match to EUVE's own spectrum, except during powerful flares. Accurate measurements of flux during flares in both the 100-150 nm and 150-300 nm ranges are impossible because EUVE's instrument underestimates these wavelengths by 20%. Assuming the FUV radiation of AU Mic is not contaminated by its nearby planetary atmospheres, the energy generated during a flare could melt the surface of AU Mic's planets, potentially resulting in water weight loss. Consequently, the FUV radiation of young stars should be a major consideration for astronomers studying exoplanetary systems.

We develop an innovative approach to describe the friction caused by radiation experienced by particles moving through a medium with mechanical resistance. We introduce an effect where the medium is warped by the motion of charged particles in a way that the Larmor formula accurately describes the energy lost due to radiation. We compare this description to the outcome predicted by a relativistic nonlinear equation that takes into consideration the friction caused by radiation, known as the Landau-Lifshitz-Purcell-Illinois or LLPI equation. We start by determining a specific form of mechanical resistance that, when used in the context of radiation friction, results in the energy lost due to radiation described by the Larmor formula. We subsequently demonstrate that, when the energy lost due to radiation is large enough to be significant, the motion of particles is influenced by both the friction caused by radiation and the mechanical resistance of the medium, and provide mathematical expressions that capture these influences accurately.

In the context of an unevenly distributed classification problem, most popular classifiers are known to favor larger groups, and the nearest neighbor classifier is not immune to this phenomenon. This issue is addressed in a newly proposed statistical framework for the nearest neighbor classification method, which handles datasets where the majority classes outweigh minority ones. Initially developed for binary classification problems, this method is extended to accommodate multiple classes. Unlike existing over-sampling techniques that involve generating fake data points, this method achieves replicable results by sidestepping pseudo observation generation. Moreover, this method has demonstrated Bayesian risk consistency when subjected to relevant conditions and shows significant improvement in its performance compared to other existing methods, all backed up by a comprehensive analysis of several reference datasets.

We employ photometry data from multiple sources to identify ultra-bright Quasi-Stellar Objects (QSOs) located at distant regions of space. By utilizing SkyMapper's DR3, along with 2MASS, VHS, and other datasets, we combine them with a comprehensive QSO catalog to analyze their distribution. As a result, our research discovers 142 novel QSOs featuring the bluest spectra, with a significant number of them located at enormous distances. By studying these QSOs, we are able to understand the rate at which supermassive black holes at the centers of galaxies grow. Moreover, we are able to provide a critical piece of information regarding the growth of supermassive black holes at early stages of universe formation. Our findings suggest that supermassive black holes at the centers of galaxies experienced significantly faster growth during the period before the universe was one billion years old compared to a previous study by Fan et al. (2006). This is supported by observations from the James Webb Space Telescope.

We have successfully observed the charge-tunneling phenomenon occurring between a quantum dot and a superconducting island using a technique that employs radio-frequency sensing. Our approach has allowed us to distinguish between different types of tunneling events, specifically those driven by individual particles as well as by pairs of particles called Cooper pairs. Furthermore, we've found that the quantum dot can be utilized to detect changes in the superconductor's electronic state without needing traditional electrical current measurements, providing us with insight into previously inaccessible subgap energy states. Our findings offer valuable insights for future research focused on detecting parity-dependent interactions between these quantum dots and superconducting islands, potentially revealing the existence of elusive Majorana modes.

Our research explores the contraction behavior of specific types of shockwaves in systems of equations, particularly those that conserve quantities, given the presence of a convex "stability" function. We establish conditions, tied to the admissible shock curves, that ensure shockwaves in a broad class of dissipative systems undergo contraction. The findings are substantial enough to encompass systems described by the Oleinik-Tsoi theory, systems of Navier-Stokes, and systems influenced by the van der Waals forces that describe flows of liquids.

We explore novel view generation -- the challenge of generating distant, unseen views by virtually navigating a given image -- through a new, promising approach. Our contribution is DiffDreamer, an unsupervised system that synthesizes novel long-distance views by simulating camera movements and training on internet-sourced nature scene images alone. Our results confirm that conditioned diffusion models excel at extending long scenes while accurately maintaining both detailed and overall scene consistency, surpassing prior methods based on GANs.

Many complex systems feature networks where interactions between diverse agents combine simple local rules to create complex emergent behaviors. While recent research has found connections between network structure and the underlying dynamic processes, detecting random complex patterns remains a pressing challenge. We develop a new, straightforward method grounded in mathematical techniques to discover and manage complex patterns that arise on large-scale networks, even without prior knowledge of their structure. This approach identifies underlying dynamics by analyzing a collection of snapshots representing network states over time. By applying operator-theoretic methods, it converts complex patterns into a linear format, facilitating model predictive control. We show that our proposed method simplifies a complex problem typically difficult to solve in large networks, transforming it into a more tractable and efficient optimization problem with a smaller number of variables.

The dynamics of a liquid film on a fiber heavily influence the morphology of synthetic and biological fibers. When subject to external forces, such as electrostatic charges, the film can experience a stability threshold, transitioning into a new equilibrium state with increased area. However, current theories fail to account for certain observed effects, like enhanced film fluctuations and the formation of nano-scales on protein fibers in certain cases. Our research revisits and expands on the Rayleigh-Plateau instability, taking into consideration the effects of slippage between the liquid and fiber wall. By examining the relevant stress scales, we identify the significance of the Couette flow within the boundary layer and demonstrate how enhanced fluctuations in the slip-induced model of the Rayleigh-Plateau instability better explain observed experiments and effects.

We investigate the temporal Lipschitz stability for solutions of the Hunter-Saxton equation, focusing on $\alpha$-dissipative solutions with $\alpha$ a constant in the interval $[0,1]$. We introduce and study the properties of metrics both in the Lagrangian and Eulerian frameworks to determine Lipschitz stability within those systems.

Evaluating scoliosis with ultrasound imaging is particularly difficult for individuals without prior experience. A newly developed robotic scanning technique combines deep learning with controlled pressure to accurately follow spinal curvature. This method was tested against manual scanning by examining the spinous process angles in 23 scoliosis patients using ultrasound. Two human evaluators measured and compared the coronal image deformity angles acquired from both robotic and manual scans. The results showed that robotic scanning yielded highly reliable results both within and between evaluators, with minimal difference compared to the manual approach in terms of coronal deformity angles. Furthermore, robotic scanning exhibited accurate intra-rater consistency, with the mean absolute deviation within an acceptable range for the vast majority of measurements. This study found that robotic scanning enables accurate and reliable scoliosis assessment through ultrasound imaging.

This paper introduces an innovative method for duration modelling in statistical parametric speech synthesis by training a recurrent model to generate phone transition probabilities frame-by-frame. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on specific distribution types and mean durations for synthesis, this new approach can model any distribution on non-negative integers. We explore a median-based output generation strategy, which offers advantages such as being more representative, robust to training data irregularities, and enabling incremental synthesis. This method is in line with a broader goal of concurrently modelling durations and acoustic features at a frame-level. Evaluations show that this approach performs comparably to state-of-the-art methods in predicting the median duration of unseen natural speech.

Identifying online hate speech is increasingly critical due to its capacity to inflict emotional and psychological harm on minority groups. A recent study from TU Berlin's research team analyzed the performance of different Natural Language Processing models on subtasks one and two of the 2021 Indo-European language shared task, which focused on detecting hate speech and derogatory content. Our team assessed the effectiveness of models that rely on word and character-based recurrent neural networks and those employing transfer learning via BERT, all of which utilized a shared task dataset. It was discovered that models employing transfer learning outperformed others across both tasks.

Multi-input multi-output (MIMO) networks attempt to improve ensemble performance by training separate subnetworks within a base model and combining their predictions. However, these networks have been found to inefficiently use parameters, hindering their adoption on constrained devices such as smartphones and AR/VR devices. This study suggests that a key issue with current MIMO frameworks lies in how they allow subnetworks to learn and share features. In response, we introduce an innovative 'unmixing' procedure for feature sharing among subnetworks, surpassing existing MIMO approaches in terms of parameter efficiency. Our method also enhances feature sharing among subnetworks, thereby improving the performance of a base model composed of random subnetworks. Moreover, we demonstrate that our feature unmixing procedure can be successfully applied in the RandNet ensemble model, enhancing feature sharing and performance. Consequently, the combination of unmixing and random subnetworks offers a promising novel paradigm for developing highly efficient feature sharing in MIMO architectures.

This study undertakes a comprehensive analysis of existing datasets pertinent to the analysis of historical documents through image-based techniques. These datasets, developed over two decades, have played a pivotal role in facilitating research and evaluation, particularly in the context of document analysis using machine learning algorithms. This investigation provides a detailed review of each dataset, encompassing its inception, characteristics, applications, and associated benchmarking studies. Furthermore, it discusses the methods employed to collect and annotate these datasets, along with the potential limitations of these studies. Based on this assessment, this work identifies areas of improvement and presents arguments in support of developing and disseminating new datasets for the research community. Ultimately, this study culminates in a comparative summary of these datasets and presents avenues for potential expansion in this area.

A key benefit of secondary encoders is enhanced position accuracy by correcting for mechanical shortcomings, like gear errors, in an industrial robot's joint. This improvement in position precision enables more precise force control, making it possible to achieve flatness of joint movements, a crucial aspect in various applications such as joint stability or linked tool stability. A novel approach to exploiting secondary encoders for flatness control in robot joints has been developed, along with a corresponding method to determine the necessary parameter estimates. This innovative solution allows for the minimization of the difference between the actual and desired positions over a specified time period. Unlike existing approaches to joint position control, this new method accurately replicates a pre-determined position trajectory. A crucial aspect of this approach is its ability to accurately replicate a pre-determined position trajectory, something that was previously unachievable. This research develops a method to accurately replicate a pre-duced motion based on real robot data, and then derives the control laws and estimation protocols for an industrial robot's joint using this approach. Finally, a comparison is made between the robot's motion accuracy when using or not using the pre-determined position trajectory, demonstrating the benefits of this novel controller.

The study of how chronic diseases evolve throughout an individual's lifetime has primarily been based on an environmental perspective, ignoring the impact of their own health conditions. This research takes a holistic approach, considering a person's ongoing health in treating acute conditions such as myocardial infarctions. By incorporating course life model trajectories, we analyze how the onset of chronic conditions like hypertension, heart disease, and diabetes influences the course of subsequent diseases and the frequency of relevant medical interventions.
